subject: Orphaned prefix attribution causing overcharge — request for credit and VAT handling
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules@brightlayer.ai>

Cc: BrightLayer Billing <billing@brightlayer.ai>, Alex Kwon <akwon@brightlayer.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected charges from orphaned ingest prefix — please advise

Hi Irene,

We're looking at the invoice for 2027-09-01 to 2027-09-13 and we see a set of charges that don't match our internal ingest metrics. Specifically, there's a cluster of requests attributed to a prefix we don't own (prefix-id: bx-ff73-orphan) starting Sep 7 that resulted in ~1.9M additional token counts (~$1,280). We've attached a small sample of our ingress logs and our copy of the billing export for that window.

We've spent time validating our keys and SDKs — nothing on our end generated that traffic. Can Redwood confirm if the prefix was re-used across tenants after a cleanup or if this looks like orphaned attribution on your side?

We need: 1) root-cause, 2) proposed remediation and credit, and 3) confirmation on VAT treatment of any retroactive credit (we are in the US but our EU subsidiary shows this on consolidated invoices).

Thanks — this is putting our month-close at risk.

Best,
Jules Martin
Head of Infrastructure — BrightLayer
J: +1 415-555-0189

Hi Jules — thanks for the detailed samples and prompt notice. Looping in Ben (billing ops) and Priyom (usage engineering) to investigate attribution and propose next steps.

Initial notes from an ops quick-check: we have a cleanup job that reclaims unused prefix allocations, but it should not retroactively reassign request attribution. That said, we've seen rare cases where idempotency keys and proxy routing produced duplicated attribution across tenants when a backend proxy failed and retried via a fallback route.

Ben / Priyom — can you take the files Jules attached and correlate with our ingress logs for prefix bx-ff73-orphan and the time windows Sep 7–9? Please confirm whether the tokens were recorded in the per-tenant ledger or as un-attributed (or marked to a recycled prefix).

Jules — we'll aim to get an initial root-cause readout within 24 hours and a proposed remediation/credit within 48 hours. On VAT: we'll confirm the treatment (credit note vs invoice reversal) once we know the jurisdictional invoice that needs adjustment; please let us know if BrightLayer prefers a credit note against the next invoice or a formal corrected invoice.

— Irene

Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from orphaned ingest prefix — please advise

Hi all — I pulled logs for the prefix bx-ff73-orphan and cross-referenced the billing-window export. Summary: 

- Root cause: A proxy failover on Sep 7 at 03:14 UTC triggered a small batch retry path that did not carry the tenant header. The requests landed on a worker assigned to a reclaimed prefix (bx-ff73-orphan) which we had not yet zeroed out in the attribution ledger — result was attribution to the reclaimed prefix instead of an un-attributed bucket.
- Scope: 1.92M input tokens and ~480k output tokens (approx) across 4 non-contiguous bursts between Sep 7 03:14 UTC and Sep 9 02:50 UTC.
- Action: We've flagged the worker to avoid further attribution to reclaimed prefixes and added a guard in the ingress pipeline to block requests that arrive without tenant headers (we will deploy this patch in the next 6 hours).

Proposed remediation / credit: refund the net usage charge for the mis-attributed tokens ($1,280.45 in usage fees) plus apply a 5% operational goodwill credit ($64.02) for the billing noise — total credit $1,344.47. We can issue a credit note against BrightLayer's next invoice or create a corrected invoice for Sep billing.

VAT treatment: Since the original invoices were issued to BrightLayer (US HQ) we recommend issuing a credit note (non-VAT) unless BrightLayer requires an EU-corrected invoice for their subsidiary. Jules, could you confirm whether this needs to reflect EU VAT? If so, please provide the EU entity name and VAT ID.

Attachments: proposed_credit_note-draft.pdf (PDF, 12KB) — draft credit note we would issue pending your acceptance and any VAT adjustments.

Ben — can you confirm the accounting flow and when the credit will appear on the account once approved?

thanks,
Priyom
